newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate slips 40 bps to 11.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate slips 40 bps to 11.1 percent.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slipped 40 basis points to 11.1 percent on Monday, despite strong demand for fresh kuna.
The day's settlements fetched 51.8 million kuna, against 57 million in supply.
Over 43 million of the total trade were new borrowings, mostly interbank call money at a steady 10.5 percent rate. Banks charged the same for loans of up to five days.
Insurers rolled over 10-day deals at nine percent.
Banks prolonged one-month loans at 15 percent, while charging 16 percent to savings banks.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday firmer at 6.0932 against the dollar and at 3.5771 versus the German mark.
